description_full: Enlight Renewable Energy Ltd operates a renewable energy platform in Israel, the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, the United States, and internationally. The company develops, finances, constructs, owns, and operates utility-scale renewable energy projects. It develops wind energy and solar energy projects, as well as energy storage projects. The company holds a portfolio of renewable energy projects that consists of approximately 20 GW of multi-technology generation capacity and 35.8 GWh of energy storage capacity. The company was incorporated in 1981 and is headquartered in Rosh HaAyin, Israel.

financial_summary: Enlight Renewable Energy Ltd. is a mid-cap utilities business with a $9.6B market cap on $489M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +36% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 18% against a 9% cost of capital, a 9-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 56% confirm genuine pricing power.
The company is burning through $1.5B of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 2.7% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 4.8% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 3.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 68% operating margin runs 47pp above the Utilities median (21%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 3.56x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+36.3% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 97 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 98% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 23% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 37% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 60% and a beta of 0.98, it moves roughly with the market.
About $12.1M trades a day, enough to build a position.
val: On multiples it looks expensive against Utilities peers: P/E 105.1 vs 20.4 and EV/EBITDA 30.0 vs 12.5 (sector median).
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of -16.0% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 7 covering analysts target $81.43 on average, 19% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 18% clears the cost of capital of 9.0% by 9pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.35).
It runs a 56% gross margin and burns cash (FCF margin -313%).
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.76x.
ROE of 10% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (5.1x equity multiplier).
hlth: The company holds more cash than debt.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.01 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
The current ratio of 0.67 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 36.5% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 17.8% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 4.8%, and institutions hold 69%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (24 sales, net $7.6M sold).
Net share issuance leaves shareholder yield negative (-2.7%), diluting holders.
people: With about 406 employees, each generates about $1.2M of revenue, 1.2x the Utilities median, and productivity has risen 36.5% a year.
Free cash flow is negative, at -$3.8M per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
